terminal.description: A shell in the top folder. Run the setup once to build the shop's folder, then go into shop and work there with git.

tasks.title: Call off Femi's unfinished merge
tasks.description:
Run `node setup.mjs` in the top folder, then work inside `shop`. On Saturday Femi started merging his branch `window-display` into `main`. Git stopped with a conflict in `index.html`, and he left it like that. Wilma has not said yes to the window display.

Call that merge off, so `main` and its files are back as they were before it started. Do not settle the conflict and do not commit it.

The check expects no merge of `window-display` to be open, `main` not to have Femi's window display, and `index.html` in the working folder to be as `main` has it.
nextSteps: Run `git status` and read its first lines: `You have unmerged paths`.
Look at `shop/index.html` in the editor: the conflict markers are there.
Call the merge off with the command from the lesson, which `git status` names too.
Run `git status` again: nothing to commit, and the markers are gone from the editor.
hints: A merge that stopped with a conflict is still open. It can be finished, or called off as if it never started.
git status prints, in brackets under its first lines, the way to call the merge off.

tasks.title: Settle the conflict in finds.html, keeping both books
tasks.description:
Femi's branch `june-finds` adds A Lamp on Gull Island to the finds, and on `main` Wilma added The Orchard Ledger at the same place. Merge `june-finds` into `main`. Git stops with a conflict in `finds.html`.

Settle it in the editor: both books stay on the list, the conflict markers go, and every other line stays as it was. Save the file.

The check reads `finds.html` (in the working folder while the merge is open, on `main` once it is finished) and expects no marker lines, both new books inside the list, and no other line lost.
nextSteps: Make sure the first task is done and you are on `main`.
Merge `june-finds` and read what Git prints: `CONFLICT` names the file.
In `shop/finds.html`, find the block between `<<<<<<<` and `>>>>>>>`.
Keep both book lines, delete the three marker lines, and save.
hints: Between the markers, the part above ======= is main's and the part below is june-finds'.
Settling means the file says what the shop wants. Here that is both lines, so only the marker lines go.
Run `git merge --no-edit june-finds`, then in the editor delete the lines that start with <<<<<<<, ======= and >>>>>>>, keep both books, and save.

videos.title: Merge conflicts, from start to finish

tasks.title: Finish the merge
tasks.description:
Tell Git the conflict is settled and make the merge commit, keeping the message Git wrote for it.

The check expects no merge left open, a merge commit on `main` that brings in `june-finds`, and `finds.html` on `main` with no conflict markers.
nextSteps: Run `git status`: `finds.html` is under Unmerged paths.
Stage the settled file: that marks it as settled.
Run `git status` again: All conflicts fixed but you are still merging.
Make the merge commit with Git's message, without an editor.
hints: Git waits for you to stage each settled file, then for a commit.
`git add` marks a file as settled. The commit takes an option that keeps Git's message.
